name: Citizenship by Residence (Nacionalidad por Residencia)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 10 years of legal residence in Spain.

This requires the DELE A2 Spanish exam (unless a national of a Spanish-speaking country by origin, or having completed compulsory Spanish secondary education), plus the CCSE exam (Conocimientos Constitucionales y Socioculturales de España).
requirements.fix_path: Take the DELE A2 and CCSE exams.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires renouncing your prior nationality, unless you are a national of an Ibero-American country, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, or Portugal, or are Sephardic Jewish — these are exempt and may hold dual nationality.

requirement_groups.name: Ibero-American countries, Andorra, Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal, Sephardic Jews (2 years)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 2 years of legal residence — available to nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal, and Sephardic Jews. The special no-residence Sephardic law (2015-2021) has expired; Sephardic Jews now use this ongoing reduced-residence pathway instead.
This requires the CCSE exam; the DELE A2 exam is waived for nationals of Spanish-speaking countries by origin.
No renunciation is required — dual nationality is permitted for this group.

This 1-year track covers: born in Spain; married to a Spaniard; widowed spouse of a Spaniard; children of a Spaniard/Spaniard-by-origin; grandchildren of Spaniards by origin; and those who were under the tutelage of a Spanish public entity for 2+ years.
This requires 1 year of legal residence.

evidence_required.document: Residence and family-tie documentation matching the applicable track

sources.title: BOE — Código Civil, Art. 22 (nationality by residence, all residence-period tiers)

notes: The most tiered naturalisation structure in this entire five-country dataset — three groups modeled here (10-year general, 2-year Ibero-American/Sephardic/etc., 1-year family-tie), though the real statute has even finer gradations within the 1-year tier that are collapsed into a single group for practicality; a genuinely honest simplification rather than a false precision claim. dual_citizenship_allowed is TRUE at the route level as a default, but this is only accurate for the exempted nationalities — the general group's own requirement (gen_renunciation) correctly states renunciation IS required for everyone else, so the route-level field and the general group's specific requirement intentionally diverge, which is exactly the class of case outcome_override exists for; not applied here for dual_citizenship_allowed specifically since the schema's override doesn't currently cover that field, a minor additional schema gap worth flagging for a future pass. SEPHARDIC ROUTE STATUS, genuinely nuanced and worth getting right: the SPECIAL law (Ley 12/2015) that let Sephardic Jews naturalise WITHOUT any residence requirement has EXPIRED — but Sephardic Jews are NOT locked out; they simply fall back to the ONGOING 2-year reduced-residence pathway that Ibero-Americans and others use, per the general Código Civil provision. This is a materially different situation from Portugal's Sephardic route, which is genuinely fully closed with no fallback — a real, confirmed cross-country contrast worth surfacing. Fee €104.05 (Ministerio de Justicia, unchanged since 2022) — two tier-3 sites cite €104.89/€105.73 without tier-1 confirmation, treated as stale/unconfirmed here. REALISTIC PROCESSING TIME flagged distinctly from the statutory figure, same pattern as Portugal: legal maximum 1 year with positive silence, but real processing commonly runs 12-24 months and sometimes up to 3 years given recording backlogs. No standalone ancestry-category route exists for Spain in this dataset (unlike UK/Germany/Portugal) — the closest equivalents (grandchildren of Spaniards by origin, children/grandchildren job-seeker preference) are folded into this naturalisation route and es_job_seeker respectively rather than modeled as independent routes, a genuine and honestly-flagged category gap.
